ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities for the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased by $3.8 million as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2025. This increase is mainly attributed to higher production-related costs due to the continued ramp-up in production that has occurred during the current year as compared to the prior year.

capex.text: During the three months ended March 31, 2026, we reported cash used in investing activities of approximately $20.7 million, which was comprised of net cash purchases of investment in debt securities of $17.2 million and cash paid for capital expenditures of $3.4 million. During the three months ended March 31, 2025, we reported cash used in investing activities of approximately $15.0 million, which was entirely comprised of cash paid for capital expenditures during that period.

intro.text: PureCycle Technologies LLC., a subsidiary of PureCycle Technologies, Inc., holds a global license for the only patented dissolution recycling technology, developed by The Procter & Gamble Company (P&G), that is designed to transform polypropylene plastic waste (designated as #5 plastic) into a continuously renewable resource. The unique purification process removes color, odor, and other impurities from #5 plastic waste resulting in our PureFive ® resin that can be recycled and reused multiple times, changing our relationship with plastic. www.purecycle.com

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

You should not rely upon forward-looking statements as predictions of future events.

PCT is a low-revenue early commercial-stage company, and may never achieve or sustain profitability, which depends on the successful commercialization and scale-up of PureFive ® resin products, and any other products PCT may develop in the future, to scale in the U.S., Europe and beyond.

In addition, PCT relies on third party software-as-a service and cloud providers for critical business functions, and any disruptions, misconfiguration or breach in these services could materially impact the Company's business.

PCT relies on its proprietary intellectual property, including registered trademarks and certain licensed intellectual property under the License Agreement and other documents to market, promote and sell PureFive ® resin products.

PCT monitors and protects against activities that might infringe, dilute, or otherwise harm its trademarks and other intellectual property and relies on the relevant patent, trademark and other laws of the U.S. and other countries.
PCT's ability to achieve commercial-scale profitability relies on its ability to commercially scale its operations.
LNOs are also FDA staff opinions rather than formal approvals, and continued reliance depends on consistency in responses.

PCT’s future success will depend on its ability to identify, hire, develop, motivate and retain highly qualified personnel for all areas of its organization, particularly research and development, recycling technology, operations and sales.

PCT’s decision to issue securities in any future offering will depend on market conditions and other factors beyond PCT’s control, which may adversely affect the amount, timing and nature of PCT’s future offerings.

Our future capital requirements will depend on many factors, including the funding and construction schedule of the Thailand, Belgium and Augusta Facilities, build-out of additional Feed PreP facilities, funding needs to support other business opportunities, funding for general corporate purposes, debt service, and other challenges or unforeseen circumstances.

Our future capital requirements will depend on many factors, including the funding and construction schedule of the Thailand, Belgium and Augusta Facilities and build-out of additional Feed PreP facilities.
The profitability of our business also depends on the availability and proximity of these raw materials to our Feed PreP facilities and Purification plants.
Entities affiliated with a greater than 5 % beneficial owner of the Company purchased $ 50.0 million aggregate principal amount of the Green Convertible Notes.
